subject: Operations
title: Economies and Diseconomies of Scale
description: A fast breakdown of Economies and Diseconomies of Scale for builders.

hook.text: A factory doubles production and cuts unit cost 20%. Then it doubles again—and costs actually rise. Scale has limits.

buildup.text: Economies of scale reduce per-unit cost as volume increases—fixed costs spread over more output.

discovery.text: Beyond a certain point, complexity, coordination problems, and bureaucracy create diseconomies of scale.

twist.text: Bigger isn't always better. Mid-sized plants often outperform mega-factories because they stay manageable.

climax.text: GM's massive plants struggled with complexity while Toyota's smaller, focused factories outperformed them.
